subject.title: Windows QuickStart defaults first chat to paid Anthropic model without credit warning

question: Should Anthropic QuickStart keep an Opus default with an explicit billing warning, switch to a lower-cost default, or require explicit model/billing confirmation before terminal hatch?
rationale: The source path is clear, but the right fix is a product policy choice for first-run defaults, paid model consent, and how much friction onboarding should add before first chat.

options.title: Require explicit model and billing confirmation
options.body: Before terminal hatch, fresh Anthropic setup-token/API-key users must confirm the selected model and acknowledge billing or credit requirements for paid models.

options.title: Use a lower-cost Anthropic default
options.body: Fresh QuickStart Anthropic setup should default to a lower-cost model while leaving Opus as an explicit opt-in in the picker.

options.title: Keep Opus with stronger warnings
options.body: The Opus default remains, but onboarding and first-chat recovery must prominently explain Anthropic billing and credit readiness before the first request.

recommendation.title: Require explicit model and billing confirmation
recommendation.body: Before terminal hatch, fresh Anthropic setup-token/API-key users must confirm the selected model and acknowledge billing or credit requirements for paid models.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter introduced the Anthropic Opus default and is the strongest history signal for the default-model policy under review.
